stem: A pipeline team needs one tool for visually cleaning messy fields without writing code, and a separate tool that automatically discovers the schema of new files and registers them in a shared metadata catalog. Which TWO tools fit these two needs respectively? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: An Athena CREATE TABLE AS SELECT query for the schema discovery
AWS Glue DataBrew for the visual cleaning
An EMR Serverless Spark job for the visual cleaning
An AWS Glue Python shell job for the schema discovery
An AWS Glue crawler for the schema discovery

rationale: DataBrew's point-and-click interface cleans messy fields without any code, and a Glue crawler scans new files, infers their schema, and registers the result in the Data Catalog. A CTAS query builds a new table from data Athena can already query through an existing table definition; it doesn't discover the schema of files nobody has cataloged yet. An EMR Serverless Spark job runs code a developer writes and offers no no-code visual cleaning interface, and a Glue Python shell job is an ETL engine that runs scripts on a single machine once data is cataloged; it is the crawler, not an ETL job, that infers the schema and writes the table definitions.
